title: Missing CSRF Token Protection on Form Submission
description:
The /add endpoint (POST method) lacks Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) token protection. The form submission accepts POST requests without any CSRF token validation. An attacker can craft a malicious webpage that, when visited by an authenticated user, will silently add bookmarks to the user's account through a cross-site request.

The vulnerability exists because:
1. No CSRF token is generated on the form
2. No CSRF token validation is performed on POST submission
3. SameSite cookie flag is not set (see cookie security finding)
4. No Origin/Referer validation is performed
impact:
An attacker can:
1. Create a malicious website with hidden form that POSTs to /add endpoint
2. Trick authenticated users into visiting the malicious site
3. Automatically add bookmarks to the victim's account without user consent
4. Potentially add malicious URLs that could be used in further attacks
5. Escalate to session hijacking combined with other vulnerabilities (XSS, cookie theft)
evidence:
POC execution demonstrates successful POST request without CSRF token:

Command: curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/add -d "name=CSRF_Test_[timestamp]&url=http://csrf-test.com"

Response Headers:
- HTTP/1.1 302 FOUND
- Location: /list
- Server: Werkzeug/3.1.3 Python/3.13.3

Key findings:
1. POST request accepted without any CSRF token validation
2. No X-CSRF-Token header required in request
3. No csrf_token field validation in form data
4. No 403 Forbidden or CSRF validation error returned
5. Request processed successfully with HTTP 302 redirect to /list
6. No Origin/Referer header validation performed

This confirms the endpoint accepts POST requests from any source without CSRF protection, enabling attackers to silently perform actions on behalf of authenticated users.
remediation:
Implement CSRF token protection:

1. **Use Flask-WTF extension** (recommended):
   ```python
   from flask_wtf.csrf import CSRFProtect
   csrf = CSRFProtect(app)
   ```

2. **Add CSRF token to form in HTML template**:
   ```html
   <form method="POST" action="/add">
       {{ csrf_token() }}
       <input type="text" name="name" required>
       <input type="url" name="url" required>
       <button type="submit">Add Bookmark</button>
   </form>
   ```

3. **Framework will automatically validate tokens on POST requests**

4. **Alternative - Manual CSRF validation**:
   - Generate random token per session
   - Include token in all forms
   - Validate token matches session on POST
   - Return 403 Forbidden if token is missing or invalid

5. **Defense-in-depth measures**:
   - Set SameSite=Strict on session cookies
   - Validate Origin/Referer headers
   - Use POST-only forms (no GET parameter mutations)

6. **Testing**:
   - Verify CSRF token is present in form HTML
   - Attempt POST without token - should receive 400 Bad Request
   - Attempt POST with invalid token - should receive 403 Forbidden
references: OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control, CWE-352 - Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), OWASP CSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet
